summary: Steel tower on Bodmin Hill near Big River, replacing a 1926 wooden tower; the Big River district towers were condemned in 2001. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.ca is not sure the tower still stands. The Big River district towers were condemned in 2001, and no source says what became of this one.

events.note: Wooden tower, 35 ft, built on Bodmin Hill six miles east of Big River.
Bruce McTaggart took over Bodmin Tower in 1945 and retired in 1962.
Old lookout torn down and replaced by a sixty-foot steel tower. The history dates the change to the end of Arnold Fonos's 1963-65 stint; the DNR report records replacement in 1965.
Stan Brettle took over as towerman in 1965 and stayed until 1979. A towermen list gives 1966-1978.
John Fonos took over the duties at Bodmin Tower in May 1999.
John Fonos retired in September 2001, when the district's towers were closed.
All fire towers in the Big River district were condemned in August 2001 over safety concerns.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Big River history, written by a towerman who knew the district, gives 1965 to 1979; a towermen list gives 1966 to 1978. The story uses the history's years and says the list differs.

The history places the 1926 tower six miles east of Big River and the tower in service in 2001 about 8 km south of Big River. The story gives both descriptions and does not assume they are the same site.

sources.title: Towers and Saskatchewan Environment, Big River and Area

notes_for_editor: The Big River district history (jkcc.com) is a first-hand account by a towerman and is the main source for dates and fate. The Firetowers list and firelookout.ca are thin on Bodmin itself. Conflicts: Brettle's years (1965-79 vs 1966-78); John Fonos's start (May 1999 in the history vs 1998 on the towermen list, not quoted in the story); the 1926 site (six miles east of town) vs the 2001 site (8 km south); coordinates differ in longitude (-106.94833 on Firelookout.ca vs 106-58-54.0 on the Firetowers list); the story gives both sets of coordinates and notes that the latitudes agree. Brief status and kind were unknown and remain so; no source says what stands now, so access is left out. Searches: one websearch.py query; the Wikipedia article for Bodmin has no tower content.
